prompts.title: Onboard your agent
prompts.description: Read the project, identify your assignment, and agree on a work area.
prompts.body:
You are joining Captain's Academy as an agent working with one of Elliott's collaborators.
Repository: Etdev2/Captains-academy-
Human collaborator: {{collaborator}}
Assigned task or issue: {{task}}

Our current collaboration phase is prototype review. A prototype is design input, not permission to implement the feature.

1. Read the current AGENTS.md, agent-resources/README.md, docs/team/HOUSE-RULES.md, docs/team/AI-OPERATING-SYSTEM.md, docs/product/DECISIONS.md, and applicable ADRs. Use the repository's pinned tools and skills.
2. Inspect open issues, pull requests, and workstream assignments. Identify your human collaborator, runtime/model, role, assigned task, dependencies, and allowed files. Ask your collaborator for missing identity or scope. Do not duplicate active work.
3. Coordinate the assignment with Sweet Potato. Follow the current builder limit. Onboarding does not add a builder slot. A direct owner instruction supersedes older repository rules only within its stated scope.
4. Before editing, record your assignment and clock in as the repository requires. Use your own branch and checkout or worktree. Never switch branches in another agent's working copy or change another workstream's files. Agree on shared interfaces before dependent work begins.
5. For an assigned design task, create mobile and desktop prototypes with fictional sample data clearly labeled. Use settled decisions and the selected Captain's Console direction where applicable. Label alternative explorations. Explain the user flow, tradeoffs, and what is static versus interactive.
6. Submit images through the existing Decision Desk inventory and feedback process. If another agent owns those files, hand over an asset pack with stable IDs, dimensions, source paths, categories, and integration instructions. Do not create another gallery or change its voting model.
7. Open a draft PR with the task, branch, exact base/head SHAs, changed files, screenshots, preview link when available, checks personally run, missing evidence, and decisions for Elliott. Do not claim a preview or test passed without observing it.
8. Wait for Elliott to select a direction and approve an implementation task before building the proposed product feature. Keep game time separate from sea time. Never make licensing eligibility claims or guarantee NMC acceptance.
9. Follow current independent-review and merge authority. Codex reviews Claude-built work; Codex-built work needs an independent reviewer. Sweet Potato may merge only a reviewed current head with no unresolved P0/P1, required Verify/Proof/Vercel checks green, and a mergeable, non-draft PR.
10. Do not push directly to main, share credentials, expose secrets, run paid APIs, or change production, access, workflows, or settings without separate authorization.

First return a short onboarding receipt: what you read, your assignment, proposed branch/worktree, allowed files, dependencies, current blockers, and the next action. Do not begin unassigned implementation.

prompts.title: Claim a workstream
prompts.description: Define ownership before anyone edits shared files.
prompts.body:
Repository: Etdev2/Captains-academy-
Human collaborator: {{collaborator}}
Proposed task or issue: {{task}}

Prepare a bounded assignment for this task. Read current repository rules and inspect active issues, PRs, branches, and assignment records. Separate design exploration from implementation.

Return the repository's compact assignment record with initiative, coordinator, runtime, role, branch, worktree, allowed writes, dependencies, status, source/constraints, expected artifact, and done criteria. Do not invent an assigned person, claim an available builder slot, or write a task is approved when it is not.

Name shared files that another workstream owns. If ownership overlaps, propose a sequence or an explicit transfer after the earlier writer stops. Do not rebase, merge, or change that workstream yourself. Ask the coordinator to confirm the assignment through the established project channel. Sending messages requires the human's authorization.

If the task is not fully specified or depends on a parked decision, state the missing decision and stop dependent work. Return a small task with observable acceptance criteria and a clear review handoff.

prompts.title: Prepare a prototype
prompts.description: Explore an assigned screen before changing the product.
prompts.body:
Repository: Etdev2/Captains-academy-
Human collaborator: {{collaborator}}
Assigned design task: {{task}}

Read the settled decisions, current design handoff, and your approved file assignment. Create static or isolated prototypes only for the assigned area. Preserve the current app, data model, game behavior, and other active branches.

Use the selected Captain's Console direction unless the task requests alternatives. Show the main user flow at 390x844 and desktop size. Label all fictional data and non-working controls. Include an empty state, the normal state, and a useful error or needs-attention state when relevant. Explain the task each screen helps the user finish.

Keep backfilled sea time labeled. Game time never counts as sea time. Use "appears to meet" with remaining requirements, never claim licensing eligibility or guaranteed NMC approval. Mark unverified regulatory content as illustrative and route it for uscg-regs review before implementation.

Return images, source files, a short README, tradeoffs, and questions for Elliott. Use stable concept IDs. For Decision Desk integration, follow its current inventory, bundled asset paths, dimensions, thumbnails, sections and feedback controls. Do not alter an owned integration file without a transfer. If another agent owns it, provide the asset pack and exact integration steps instead.

Run the applicable checks and distinguish rendered screenshots from image concepts. Open a draft PR and hand it off for design review. Elliott's selection must be recorded before an approved implementation task starts.

prompts.title: Review prototypes together
prompts.description: Turn feedback into a specific design decision.
prompts.body:
Repository: Etdev2/Captains-academy-
Reviewer or collaborator: {{collaborator}}
Prototype set or task: {{task}}

Review the assigned prototypes in the existing Decision Desk using its current feedback controls. Read the task and what each concept is trying to solve. Do not change the app or the voting model.

For each concept, assess whether the main task is clear, the next action is easy to find, mobile text and controls are usable, important status has words as well as color, and empty/error states make sense. Separate visual preference from broken behavior and from unanswered product decisions.

Attach each observation to the stable concept ID and a specific screen or location. Say what confused you, its consequence, and a concrete change to try. Do not treat the number of votes as automatic approval.

Return a short comparison, unresolved questions, and a recommendation. Elliott makes the selection. Record the selected concept/version and the reason through the established process. If nobody has selected a direction, leave it undecided. Create or propose the next implementation task only after that decision; do not start implementation from this review prompt.

prompts.title: Hand off your work
prompts.description: Make it possible for the next person to continue without guessing.
prompts.body:
Repository: Etdev2/Captains-academy-
Human collaborator: {{collaborator}}
Task or issue: {{task}}

Prepare a handoff for your assigned workstream. Follow the current time-card, proof, and review rules. Clock out before the final proof rewrite. Push only your assigned branch.

Include:
- The issue/spec, branch, exact base/head SHAs, PR and preview links.
- What changed, why, and which files you owned.
- Screenshots of the real artifact when behavior changed.
- Commands personally run and their results. Separate local tests, CI, builder transcripts, missing evidence, and failures.
- Any unresolved P0/P1, and one linked follow-up issue for P2/P3 findings when applicable.
- Remaining decisions, dependencies, and the next person/action. A handoff transfers information, not file ownership.

Run the project's required verification steps without skipping them. Generate the proof bundle with the correct ticket and run check-proof.sh. If the environment blocks a check, report that plainly and keep the PR draft. Do not fabricate PASS evidence.

Do not merge, deploy, change production, or grant access. The independent reviewer and authorized coordinator handle review and merge under current project rules. Do not describe work as merge-ready until the reviewed current head satisfies every required gate.

prompts.title: Hill climb a live prototype
prompts.description: Lower the tap count of one live variant's main task, step by step, with a script deciding each step. Copy it from the Hill climb button on the Decision Desk, which fills in the category, variant and concept.
prompts.body:
You are improving one live prototype on Captain's Academy's Decision Desk by hill climbing. Category: {{category}}. Variant: {{variant}}. Concept: {{conceptId}}.

Before you edit anything: get an assignment through Sweet Potato, clock in on a time card in agent-resources/timecards/, and work on your own branch. Read GLOSSARY.md and docs/team/HOUSE-RULES.md.

The goal is to lower the climb score for this category's main task without failing the gate. You may change only the climbed variant's folder and its task path file. Do not edit the scoring script, the end-state checks, or the A/B/C variants.

1. Copy variant {{variant}} to climb 1 and run scripts/hill-climb-score.mjs on it. That is step 0. Record it.
2. For each step, up to 5:
   a. Reread the trajectory: every earlier candidate, sorted from worst to best score, each with a one-line description of the change and its JSON result.
   b. Propose 3 different candidates that you expect to score lower than the current best. Each must change something different from the ones already tried. Before you edit, write one sentence per candidate on why it should save taps.
   c. Build and score each candidate. Never estimate a score. Run the script.
   d. Keep the best candidate only if it passes the gate and beats the current best. Otherwise keep the current best.
3. Stop after step 5, or after 2 steps in a row with no improvement.
4. Verify before you report. Rerun the script on the 1 to 3 best climbed variants. List any claim in your report that the script output does not support, and remove it.
5. Capture desktop and iPhone screenshots of each kept climbed variant, add them to docs/prototypes/inventory.json as cl-climb-{{category}}-{{variant}}-<n>-desktop and -iphone, and follow "Changing the inventory" in docs/prototypes/decision-board.md.
6. Run bash scripts/verify.sh, commit a proof bundle with scripts/write-proof.sh, and open a draft pull request.

Report in this format:
- The trajectory table: step, candidate, change, gate, taps, median seconds, kept (yes or no).
- The climbed variants added, with their URLs and concept ids.
- What the climb could not improve, and why.
- A plain-language version, described below.

The plain-language version is for a reader with no design or coding background, such as a first-year college student in a liberal arts program. Put it first in the report and in the pull request description, under the heading "In plain language". Rules:
- 150 to 250 words of whole sentences. No tables, file names, ids, code or abbreviations.
- Explain any needed term (tap target, contrast) in the same sentence that uses it.
- Cover, in this order: what the screen is for and who uses it; what you measured and why fewer taps matters to a mariner on a moving deck with one hand free; what the climb tried; what worked and what did not; what happens next (the team votes, and nothing is built yet).
- Every number in it must match the trajectory table. Check this before you report.

Example of the tone and length. The numbers in it are invented. Use your real results.

> This screen is where a boat crew member records that a stretch of time at sea has started, which counts toward their captain's license. They often do it standing on a moving deck with one hand holding on, so every extra tap matters. We counted how many taps it takes to finish that job. The original design took 6 taps. We tried 15 small redesigns, three at a time, and kept a change only when it lowered the count. Every version also had to pass two basic checks: each button had to be big enough to hit with a gloved thumb, and the text had to stand out from its background so it can be read in bright sun. The best version takes 3 taps, because it puts the check-in button on the first screen instead of two screens in. Two ideas failed. One made the buttons too small, and one hid information the check-in needs. None of this is in the real app yet. The team will look at the new versions next to the original and vote on which direction to take.

A climbed variant is design input. The team dot-votes on it. It does not approve building anything.
